page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is an entry-level shared instance belonging to the burstable t5 family. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration provides 2 burstable vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core via hyper-threading. The CPU includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage and features a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate low baseline computational and I/O capabilities, reflecting the burstable CPU credit architecture. Stress-ng returned scores of 1057.79 for single-core and 2090.03 for multi-core performance, both placing in the bottom tier. Geekbench testing mirrors these findings with a single-core score of 870.0 and a multi-core score of 1493.0. In memory throughput, the server achieved 16.3 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 14.44 GB/sec write bandwidth. Operational throughput yielded 2.54 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 1.48 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

Because computing resources are governed by burstable CPU allocations and lack dedicated local storage, the instance trades continuous compute power for baseline resource efficiency. It is ill-suited for sustained compute, heavy compilation, or intensive database operations. Instead, Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is positioned for lightweight workloads with intermittent CPU utilization, such as low-traffic web applications, non-critical background automation, microservices, and development or testing environments.
